stock.counterargument: Growth decelerated against the previous quarter, so the trend in the numbers is already turning.
invalidation: Quarterly revenue growth falling below +12.2%, the rate it was running at the quarter before.
Cash conversion dropping below 1.0×, meaning earnings stop being backed by cash.
A close below the 200-session average, which stood at $171.95 on the decision date.
risks: The share count is from 2026-06-30, 135 days older than the price, so the market capitalisation carries that staleness.
The most recent filing covers a period ending 2026-06-30, 135 days before the decision date.
Point-in-time fundamentals are built from filings accepted up to 2026-11-12.

earnings.basis: the same fiscal quarter's announcement a year earlier (2026-02-25) plus 364 days

stock.rule: Universe: every US-listed common stock on NYSE, Nasdaq or NYSE American — about 4,700 names from Nasdaq Trader's own file. Eligible means: priced at $5 or more, median daily turnover of $20M or more over 60 sessions, at least 253 sessions of history, a 10-Q or 10-K whose period ended within 200 days, close above the 200-session average, volatility inside the day's 85th percentile, debt no more than 6× operating cash flow, no results announced in the last 2 sessions, and no position already open in the stock or a fourth in the same SIC division. Eligible candidates are then ranked on equally weighted z-scores within their sector group, over the signals that are defined for that group. One position per session, held 21 sessions, a twenty-first of capital each, 10 basis points of cost each way. Fundamentals are read as they stood on the decision date, never as they read today. The score is a ranking position among that day's eligible candidates. It is not a probability, a price target, or a forecast of any return.
stock.validation: The held-out window has not been opened. No claim of an edge is made or implied.

stories.title: Learn With Mentor AI: Working Through a Coding Exercise
stories.excerpt: Learn how to use Mentor AI on a Real Python coding exercise. Ask why a test failed, get hints instead of the answer, and check your understanding.
stories.lead:
Real Python has hundreds of coding exercises that let you practice what you’ve learned in a tutorial or course. Each exercise gives you a task, a code editor, and a set of tests that check your solution. When all the tests pass, you’ve solved the exercise.

Sometimes, though, the tests keep failing and you can’t figure out why. At that point, it’s tempting to open the solution and copy it. The tests turn green, but you don’t learn much from it.

stories.title: Chris Van Hollen says he will challenge Chuck Schumer for Senate majority leader
stories.excerpt: Van Hollen, a progressive from Maryland, said voters sent a clear message in the midterm elections — that they want "change from the status quo."
stories.lead:
Sen. Chris Van Hollen of Maryland has announced he will challenge New York's Chuck Schumer for the job of Senate majority leader, pushing the party into a fresh debate over its future just days after sweeping victories in the midterm elections.

Van Hollen made the announcement on Thursday, saying voters sent a clear message in the midterms — that they want "change from the status quo."

"It's now on us to meet this moment, and to do that we need new leadership," Van Hollen said in a statement. "This is not about any one person — it's about answering the call of the American people. That is why I'm running for Senate Majority Leader."

Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, who is under scrutiny over exports of sensitive Nvidia AI chips to China, has also been summoned to appear before the Senate Banking Committee in December.

stories.title: Is Outlook down? Widespread outage hits Microsoft email and other apps
stories.excerpt: A widespread outage has hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts.
stories.lead:
A widespread outage hit Microsoft platforms including Outlook on Thursday, with many users encountering trouble using their email accounts and other errors across the tech giant's suite of apps.

Nearly 130,000 users on outage tracker Downdetector reported problems accessing Outlook just after 1 p.m. ET. New reports have since fallen from that peak, but many said they couldn't send and receive emails or had trouble loading their inboxes altogether.

Thousands also reported issues with Microsoft's workplace messaging app Teams, as well as its AI assistant Copilot and wider Microsoft 365 services.

stories.title: Australian footballers will not be charged after hotel incident, police say
stories.excerpt: Four Sydney Swans players had been under investigation after an alleged sexual assault after a game in Melbourne.
stories.lead:
Four top Australian Football League (AFL) players who were investigated in relation to an alleged sexual assault at a hotel in Melbourne earlier this year will not be charged, police have said.

After a "thorough investigation and based on legal advice" police would not proceed with criminal charges due to "insufficient evidence", police said in a statement.

Four Sydney Swans players - Isaac Heeney, James Jordon, Chad Warner and Nick Blakey, who now plays for North Melbourne - had been suspended for the rest of the season over the incident in August.

stories.lead:
Midterms coverage: Live results | What to know | Stories around the countryStay connected: NPR Politics Podcast | NPR Politics newsletter | NPR app

Democratic state Sen. Cindy Holscher will hold onto the Kansas governor's office for her party after defeating Republican Ty Masterson, according to a race call by the Associated Press.

Masterson, the president of the state Senate, was endorsed by President Trump. Of the 36 elections for governor across the country, Kansas was seen as the most likely to flip from Democratic to Republican control.

stories.lead:
Among the 20 managers with more than 290 matches in the Premier League, only the five “big beasts” of Alex Ferguson, Arsène Wenger, José Mourinho, Jürgen Klopp and Pep Guardiola have better points-per-game averages than Mauricio Pochettino. He is an elite manager.

Pochettino took over Southampton midway through their first season back in the top flight (2012-13) after the club spent seven years in the lower leagues. In his only full campaign, they finished eighth. He led Tottenham to second in 2016-17, third in the seasons either side, and reached the 2019 Champions League final. His presence lifted those clubs.
